sections.title: Welcome and about us
sections.body:
## Welcome

Welcome to Ridgeline. This handbook explains how we work together, what you can expect from us and what we expect from you.

## About us

Ridgeline machines precision valve housings and hydraulic components in Dayton and Fort Wayne for industrial customers, and has done so since 1994.

## About this handbook

This handbook is a guide, not a contract of employment. Ridgeline may change its policies; when it does, the new version is published here and you will be asked to read it. If a policy here conflicts with a written agreement or the law, the agreement or the law applies.

Questions go to Lena Park (HR and payroll).

sections.title: Employment basics
sections.body:
## At-will employment

Employment with Ridgeline in Ohio and Indiana is at will: either side may end it at any time, with or without notice.

## Equal opportunity

Ridgeline makes employment decisions without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status or any other status protected by law.

## Employee classifications

- **Full-time:** scheduled 32 or more hours a week.
- **Part-time:** scheduled fewer than 32 hours a week.
- **Exempt and non-exempt:** non-exempt employees are paid overtime as the law requires.

## Introductory period

The first 90 days are an introductory period to learn the job; benefits start on the first of the month after 30 days.

sections.title: Code of conduct
sections.body:
## How we treat each other

We expect honesty, respect and safe work from everyone. Raise concerns early; no one will be punished for a concern raised in good faith.

## Conflicts of interest

Tell HR about any outside work, investment or relationship that could affect your decisions here.

## Gifts

Do not accept gifts from suppliers or customers worth more than $50, or any cash.

## Reporting concerns

Report concerns to your supervisor, HR, or the anonymous line, 1-800-555-0144.

sections.title: Anti-harassment and anti-discrimination
sections.body:
## Our commitment

Harassment and discrimination are not tolerated, whether by employees, supervisors, customers, suppliers or visitors.

## What to do

If you experience or see harassment, report it to HR or the plant manager. You may skip anyone involved. Reports are investigated promptly and kept as confidential as the investigation allows.

## No retaliation

Retaliation against anyone who reports in good faith or takes part in an investigation is itself a violation of this policy.

sections.title: Hours, timekeeping and pay
sections.body:
## Work hours

Normal hours are first shift 6:00–14:30 and second shift 14:30–23:00, Monday to Friday. Your supervisor sets your schedule.

## Recording time

Non-exempt employees record all time worked in the timesheet and submit it every week for approval. Working off the clock is not allowed.

## Overtime

Overtime must be approved in advance by your supervisor and is paid as the law requires.

## Paydays

Pay is every two weeks, on Friday. Report any pay error to HR right away.

sections.title: Paid time off and holidays
sections.body:
## Paid time off

Full-time employees earn 80 hours of paid time off a year, accrued each pay period. Up to 40 unused hours carry over; unused time is not paid out.

## Requesting time off

Ask your supervisor at least 14 days ahead, except for illness or emergencies.

## Holidays

The company observes: New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving and the day after, Christmas Eve and Christmas Day.

## Leave of absence

Family and medical leave follows the FMLA; military leave follows USERRA. Ask HR before any leave longer than a week.

sections.title: Safety
sections.body:
## Everyone's responsibility

Follow safe work procedures, wear the required protective equipment, and stop any job you believe is unsafe.

## Report every incident

Report injuries, near misses and unsafe conditions the same day in the safety section of this system, or to your supervisor.

## Qualified work only

Operate and maintain only the equipment you are qualified for. The system shows your current qualifications.

## Drugs and alcohol

Working under the influence of alcohol or drugs is prohibited. Testing follows an injury requiring treatment and reasonable suspicion.

sections.title: Technology, data and confidentiality
sections.body:
## Company systems

Company devices, email and systems are for business use. Brief personal use on breaks is fine. Activity on them may be monitored.

## Passwords and access

Keep your sign-in private and never share it. Report a lost device or a suspicious message to HR at once.

## Confidential information

Customer, supplier, pricing, design and employee information stays confidential during and after your employment.

sections.title: Business expenses
sections.body:
## Summary

The company reimburses reasonable expenses incurred for business. Submit them as expense reports in this system; the full rules are in the Expense and travel policy. Approved expenses are repaid with the next payroll.

catalogue.label: Beyond a control limit
catalogue.description: One point above the upper or below the lower control limit.

catalogue.label: 9 in a row on one side
catalogue.description: Nine points in a row on the same side of the center line: the process has shifted.

catalogue.label: 6 in a row rising or falling
catalogue.description: Six points in a row each higher (or lower) than the last: a trend such as tool wear.

catalogue.label: 2 of 3 beyond 2σ
catalogue.description: Two of three points in a row more than two sigma from the center, on the same side.

catalogue.label: Range beyond its limit
catalogue.description: The spread within a subgroup (or between readings) above its control limit.

catalogue.label: Out of tolerance
catalogue.description: A measurement outside the drawing tolerance (not a control-chart rule: the part is bad).

catalogue.label: 4 of 5 beyond 1σ
catalogue.description: Four of five points in a row more than one sigma from the center, on the same side: a small shift.

catalogue.label: 8 in a row beyond 1σ
catalogue.description: Eight points in a row more than one sigma from the center, on either side: a mixture of two processes.

catalogue.label: 15 in a row within 1σ
catalogue.description: Fifteen points in a row hugging the center line: limits too wide, or data averaged or stratified.

catalogue.label: 14 in a row alternating
catalogue.description: Fourteen points in a row alternating up and down: over-adjustment or two alternating sources.

b.label: Sites (properties, stores, plants)
b.description: One row per property, store, plant or warehouse with its address and optional group (portfolio, region, district). Administrators only.

fields.label: Site code

b.label: Assets / equipment register
b.description: Equipment, components, tools and facility systems. Locations are created from paths like "Bldg 2 > Line 3"; components reference their parent by tag.

fields.label: Location path
fields.description: Hierarchy separated by ">" or "/", e.g. "Building 2 > Line 3". Missing locations are created.

b.label: Parts / spares master
b.description: Maintenance spares and consumables. Load on-hand quantities with the stock_balances target; unmapped columns are kept in custom fields.

fields.label: Purchase unit
fields.description: The unit it is bought in when that is not the stock unit (BOX, CASE, DRUM); with "Stock units per purchase unit"

fields.label: Stock units per purchase unit
fields.description: How many stock units are in one purchase unit (a box of 10: 10)

b.label: Storerooms
b.description: Each place stock is kept: code, name, site. Bins are a column on the stock balances, not locations of their own.

b.label: Stock on hand (opening balances)
b.description: On-hand quantity per part and storeroom, with optional bin and reorder settings. Parts and storerooms must exist first.

fields.label: Lot or serial number
fields.description: Required for lot- or serial-tracked parts; one row per lot

b.label: Equipment parts lists (spares per machine)
b.description: Which spare parts each machine uses, how many are installed, where, and which are critical. Matches parts by part number or manufacturer part number.

b.label: Meter readings
b.description: Readings of hour, cycle or mileage meters per machine: asset tag, meter name, reading, date. Applied oldest first; a reading below an earlier one is refused. The last reading per meter is what meter-based preventive maintenance counts from.

b.label: Preventive maintenance plans
b.description: One row per machine and task: asset tag, task, how often (days, or a word like monthly or "every 6 months"; or a meter and its interval), hours, and when it was last done so the next due date continues the schedule. Machines must be loaded first. A plan that already exists is left as it is.

fields.label: Plan code
fields.description: Optional; made from the asset tag and task when blank

fields.label: How often
fields.description: Days (90), or words: weekly, monthly, quarterly, annual, "every 6 months"

fields.label: Meter
fields.description: For meter-based plans: the meter name, for example hours

b.label: Bills of materials
b.description: Components and quantity per unit for manufactured parts, flat or indented. Lines land on a draft revision for review; parts must exist first.

fields.label: Parent part
fields.description: The part being made. Leave unmapped for indented BOMs that use a level column.

b.label: Work centers
b.description: A machine group, cell or station where operations are done: code, name, site, the machines in it (asset tags separated by semicolons), scheduled hours a week and the number of machines or crews. Machines must be loaded first.

fields.label: Machines (asset tags)
fields.description: Asset tags separated by semicolons or commas

b.label: Routings (operations)
b.description: One row per operation: the part made, operation number, work center, description, setup minutes and run minutes per unit. Parts and work centers must exist first. Operations go on the part's draft revision, alongside its bill of material, for a person to review and release.

b.label: Suppliers / vendors
b.description: Vendor list (code, name, contact, terms). Bank and tax details stay in the accounting system; do not import them.

fields.label: Trades (contractors)
fields.description: Comma or semicolon separated, e.g. "plumbing; hvac"

b.label: Supplier price list
b.description: Price, lead time and supplier part number per supplier and part. Suppliers and parts must exist first. One row per supplier and part.

fields.label: Price unit
fields.description: The unit the price is per, when the supplier sells in boxes, cases or drums; blank means the stock unit

b.label: Open purchase orders
b.description: Orders not yet fully received, one row per line: order number, supplier, part (or description), quantity ordered and already received, price, due date. Suppliers and parts must exist first. Received quantities are history; stock on hand is loaded as a count.

b.label: Supplier delivery history
b.description: Past purchase order lines with due and received dates and rejected quantities, for supplier scorecards. Suppliers must be loaded first.

fields.label: PO and line
fields.description: Unique per supplier, e.g. 4500123-10

b.label: Spend history
b.description: Monthly spend by account from the previous accounting system, for history analysis and budgets. Rows are classified into spend categories through the account mapping or a category column.

fields.label: Site
fields.description: Site code; the import's site when blank

fields.label: Department
fields.description: Department code or name (optional)

fields.label: Spend category
fields.description: Spend category code or name; overrides the account mapping

b.label: Budget lines
b.description: One row per site, department, spend category and month: the budget name and year, then the amount. A sheet with a column per month loads through the "wide to long" option. The budget is created as a draft when it does not exist; approved budgets are not changed.

fields.label: Month
fields.description: January or Jan, or 1 to 12 (calendar month)

b.label: Chart of accounts
b.description: Account number, name and type from the accounting system. Adds to the starter chart; accounts that already have entries keep their type. Set the books up first (Books → Settings).

fields.label: Detail type
fields.description: Optional: bank, accounts receivable, inventory, fixed asset, credit card, accounts payable, cost of goods and so on. Worked out from the name when blank.

b.label: Opening balances (trial balance)
b.description: The previous accounting system's trial balance, as opening balances in the built-in books.

fields.label: Account
fields.description: Account number or name; "1000 · Checking" style labels are matched by either part

fields.label: Account name
fields.description: Used to create an account the chart does not have (with a type)

fields.label: Account type
fields.description: Needed only to create a missing account

fields.label: As of
fields.description: Defaults to the day before the books start

b.label: Bank and card transactions
b.description: Statement lines from your bank or card export, into the books' banking queue to match or categorize.

fields.label: Bank account
fields.description: Account code, name or last four digits; the default bank account when blank

fields.label: Amount (signed)
fields.description: Positive money in, negative money out

b.label: Customers / accounts
b.description: Customer and prospect accounts with an optional primary contact per row. Bank and tax IDs stay in accounting; do not import them.

b.label: Sales items and price list
b.description: Products and services you quote and invoice: code, description, kind, unit, list price, cost, and the part it is made as. A part number links the item to stock and production.

b.label: Sales opportunities
b.description: Your pipeline from the CRM or a spreadsheet: customer, title, stage, amount, expected close and the person who owns it. Customers must exist first. A deal that was lost needs the reason.

b.label: Open customer invoices
b.description: Invoices still unpaid at the cutover date (an aging report): invoice number, customer, dates and the amount still owed. Customers must exist first. Paid history is not needed. With the built-in books, load the trial balance without the receivables line: these invoices provide it.

b.label: Open supplier bills
b.description: Bills still unpaid at the cutover date (a payables aging): supplier, bill number, dates and the amount still owed. Suppliers must exist first. With the built-in books, load the trial balance without the payables line: these bills provide it.

b.label: Customer forecasts
b.description: Quantities per customer, part and month into the customer's draft forecast at the chosen site. Activate the draft after reviewing it.

b.label: Consumables and chemicals usage
b.description: How much of a consumable or chemical a work center uses per machine hour, per part made, or per month. Feeds the material plan and its cost forecast.

fields.label: Work center code
fields.description: Blank for site-wide monthly usage

fields.label: Per (how many hours, parts or months)
fields.description: Default 1

b.label: Rental units (beds, size, market rent)
b.description: Makes existing spaces rentable with their type, bedrooms, bathrooms, size and market rent. Load units as assets (class space) first.

b.label: Leases (rent roll)
b.description: Leases in force or signed for the future, from a rent roll export. Units must be rental units first. Balances owed stay in the old system or accounting; this loads the leases, not the ledger.

b.label: Maintenance history (legacy work orders)
b.description: Closed or open work orders from a previous CMMS, spreadsheet or paper log. Legacy numbers are kept; labor is attached when the technician can be matched.

fields.label: Parts and contractor cost
fields.description: Cost of the job other than in-house labor (parts, outside services); used for repair-or-replace

fields.label: Downtime hours (reference only)
fields.description: Kept as reference on the work order. Import a downtime log to build utilization history.

b.label: Downtime / state log
b.description: Historical machine state intervals (e.g. a downtime spreadsheet) used for availability and utilization history. Overlapping intervals for the same asset are rejected.

b.label: Condition limits (coolers, freezers)
b.description: What is logged on which equipment, with its limits and how often: e.g. walk-in cooler 33–41°F every 12 h. Equipment must exist first.

b.label: Condition readings (temperature logs)
b.description: Readings for condition points already set up on assets (e.g. walk-in cooler 33–41°F). Out-of-limit readings raise requests as they would in the app.

fields.label: Measure
fields.description: Defaults to temperature

b.label: SPC characteristics
b.description: One row per measured characteristic: code, name, unit, nominal and limits, subgroup size, how often, and optionally the part and the gauge. Load these before the measurements.

fields.label: Chart type
fields.description: variables (measurements) or p, np, c, u (counts)

b.label: SPC measurements
b.description: Subgroups of measurements for set-up characteristics (one row per subgroup). Control-chart signals and out-of-tolerance values alert quality as they would when typed in.

fields.label: Values
fields.description: One value, or the subgroup separated by spaces or semicolons

fields.label: Sample size (attribute charts)
fields.description: Parts or units inspected, for p and u charts

b.label: Calibration plans and last calibration
b.description: One row per instrument (already loaded as equipment): how often it is calibrated, the tolerance, and when it was last calibrated, by whom, with the certificate. The next due date continues from the last calibration. Past results are recorded as history: they do not raise nonconformances or take instruments out of service.

fields.label: Calibrate every
fields.description: Days, or words: annual, every 6 months

b.label: Nonconformance history
b.description: Past nonconformance reports (NCR, reject, deviation logs): your number, date, what happened, severity, the part and quantity, the disposition and cost, and when it was closed. Brought in as records for trends and audits; the workflow does not run.

b.label: Safety incident history
b.description: Past incident and near-miss logs: your number, date, what kind, what happened, severity, whether it was recordable, days away or restricted. Brought in as closed records so incident rates and trends cover the earlier years. Personal injury detail is not needed.

b.label: Qualifications (definitions)
b.description: The skills and certificates you track: code, name, how long each stays valid, and whether it is safety critical or needs a practical sign-off. Load these before qualification records.

b.label: Qualification records (legacy training matrix)
b.description: One row per person and qualification, or a wide training matrix (one column per qualification) using the unpivot option. Qualifications must be defined first.

b.label: Earning codes (payroll)
b.description: What hours are called on a timesheet (regular, overtime, holiday, sick) and the code your payroll provider uses for each in its import file.

b.label: Timesheet history
b.description: Past hours: employee number, date, earning code, hours (one row per person, day and code). Brought in as already paid: frozen, never exported to payroll again. Employees and earning codes must exist first.

b.label: Expense categories
b.description: Categories people claim against (meals, lodging, mileage): code, name, per-item and per-day limits, the amount over which a receipt is required.

sections.title: Welcome and about us
sections.body:
## Welcome

Welcome to Ridgeline. This handbook explains how we work together, what you can expect from us and what we expect from you.

## About us

Ridgeline machines precision valve housings and hydraulic components in Dayton and Fort Wayne for industrial customers, and has done so since 1994.

## About this handbook

This handbook is a guide, not a contract of employment. Ridgeline may change its policies; when it does, the new version is published here and you will be asked to read it. If a policy here conflicts with a written agreement or the law, the agreement or the law applies.

Questions go to Lena Park (HR and payroll).

sections.title: Employment basics
sections.body:
## At-will employment

Employment with Ridgeline in Ohio and Indiana is at will: either side may end it at any time, with or without notice.

## Equal opportunity

Ridgeline makes employment decisions without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status or any other status protected by law.

## Employee classifications

- **Full-time:** scheduled 32 or more hours a week.
- **Part-time:** scheduled fewer than 32 hours a week.
- **Exempt and non-exempt:** non-exempt employees are paid overtime as the law requires.

## Introductory period

The first 90 days are an introductory period to learn the job; benefits start on the first of the month after 30 days.

sections.title: Code of conduct
sections.body:
## How we treat each other

We expect honesty, respect and safe work from everyone. Raise concerns early; no one will be punished for a concern raised in good faith.

## Conflicts of interest

Tell HR about any outside work, investment or relationship that could affect your decisions here.

## Gifts

Do not accept gifts from suppliers or customers worth more than $50, or any cash.

## Reporting concerns

Report concerns to your supervisor, HR, or the anonymous line, 1-800-555-0144.

sections.title: Anti-harassment and anti-discrimination
sections.body:
## Our commitment

Harassment and discrimination are not tolerated, whether by employees, supervisors, customers, suppliers or visitors.

## What to do

If you experience or see harassment, report it to HR or the plant manager. You may skip anyone involved. Reports are investigated promptly and kept as confidential as the investigation allows.

## No retaliation

Retaliation against anyone who reports in good faith or takes part in an investigation is itself a violation of this policy.

sections.title: Hours, timekeeping and pay
sections.body:
## Work hours

Normal hours are first shift 6:00–14:30 and second shift 14:30–23:00, Monday to Friday. Your supervisor sets your schedule.

## Recording time

Non-exempt employees record all time worked in the timesheet and submit it every week for approval. Working off the clock is not allowed.

## Overtime

Overtime must be approved in advance by your supervisor and is paid as the law requires.

## Paydays

Pay is every two weeks, on Friday. Report any pay error to HR right away.

sections.title: Paid time off and holidays
sections.body:
## Paid time off

Full-time employees earn 80 hours of paid time off a year, accrued each pay period. Up to 40 unused hours carry over; unused time is not paid out.

## Requesting time off

Ask your supervisor at least 14 days ahead, except for illness or emergencies.

## Holidays

The company observes: New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving and the day after, Christmas Eve and Christmas Day.

## Leave of absence

Family and medical leave follows the FMLA; military leave follows USERRA. Ask HR before any leave longer than a week.

sections.title: Safety
sections.body:
## Everyone's responsibility

Follow safe work procedures, wear the required protective equipment, and stop any job you believe is unsafe.

## Report every incident

Report injuries, near misses and unsafe conditions the same day in the safety section of this system, or to your supervisor.

## Qualified work only

Operate and maintain only the equipment you are qualified for. The system shows your current qualifications.

## Drugs and alcohol

Working under the influence of alcohol or drugs is prohibited. Testing follows an injury requiring treatment and reasonable suspicion.

sections.title: Technology, data and confidentiality
sections.body:
## Company systems

Company devices, email and systems are for business use. Brief personal use on breaks is fine. Activity on them may be monitored.

## Passwords and access

Keep your sign-in private and never share it. Report a lost device or a suspicious message to HR at once.

## Confidential information

Customer, supplier, pricing, design and employee information stays confidential during and after your employment.

sections.title: Business expenses
sections.body:
## Summary

The company reimburses reasonable expenses incurred for business. Submit them as expense reports in this system; the full rules are in the Expense and travel policy. Approved expenses are repaid with the next payroll.

b.description: Tracked stock that is expired, expires within the window, or is on hold, by lot and storeroom, with its value at average cost.

b.name: FMEA risk register
b.description: High-priority failure modes still open across approved and draft FMEAs, recommended actions overdue, FMEAs past their review date, and equipment failure modes that happened more often than rated.

b.name: Continuity readiness
b.description: Critical processes with an approved continuity plan, whether each has recovered within its RTO in a timed exercise, reviews and exercises overdue, and gaps found in live records (skills, people, suppliers, equipment).

b.name: Equipment reliability (MTBF / MTTR)
b.description: Failures, mean time between failures and mean time to repair per asset, against the previous period, with bad actors and repeat failure codes.

b.name: Service levels by site and contractor
b.description: Work orders responded to and completed within the targets for their priority, by site or by contractor, with contractor spend over not-to-exceed.

b.name: Rent roll and occupancy
b.description: Every rental unit with its renter, lease dates, rent and balance; occupancy, rent lost to vacancy, past-due rent, leases ending soon and unit turns running late.

b.name: Store standards and conditions
b.description: Per site: the latest visit score against the one before, critical misses, open fixes, condition readings taken on time, and excursions out of limits with how long they lasted.

b.name: Capacity and material plan
b.description: Customer forecasts and firm orders turned into work-center load against demonstrated capacity, month by month, with the bottleneck, material shortfalls and the assumptions made.

b.name: Process control and capability
b.description: Each measured characteristic: whether its control chart signals, the open signals waiting for an investigation, and short- and long-term capability against the tolerance.

b.name: Supplier performance
b.description: Each supplier's on-time delivery, rejected parts per million, price against quote and open corrective action requests over the period, worst first.

b.name: Continuous improvement
b.description: Ideas and improvements by stage, results measured against their baseline, and savings: estimated by owners, validated by someone else.

b.name: Repair or replace
b.description: For each asset with a replacement cost: what keeping it is expected to cost this year (maintenance and priced downtime, on its trend) against the equivalent annual cost of a new one.

b.name: Employee expenses
b.description: Expense spend by category and department over the period, policy exceptions approved, reports waiting for approval and approved reports not yet reimbursed.

b.name: Budget against actual
b.description: Spend to date against the approved budget by site, department and category, with open commitments, a forecast for the year and lines over or heading over budget.

b.name: Profit and loss
b.description: Income, cost of goods sold, expenses and net income from the built-in books for a period.

b.name: Balance sheet
b.description: Assets, liabilities and equity from the built-in books as of a date, with this year's net income.

b.name: Business cases
b.description: Opportunity pro formas with their base case: NPV, IRR, payback, funding needed and status, approved and waiting first.

b.name: Labor productivity
b.description: Output per direct labor hour by part against its standard rate, labor efficiency (standard hours earned ÷ direct labor hours) by operator, work center and week, and how much paid time went to direct work.

b.name: Document master list
b.description: Every controlled document with its revision in force, effective date, approver, owner and status; external documents with the issuer's number and revision.

b.name: Specification reviews
b.description: New revisions of customer specifications and standards: received, due, decided, on time or late, the outcome and the follow-up revisions of our documents.

b.name: Read and understood
b.description: For each document revision that required it: people who had to read it, who acknowledged it and when, and who is overdue.

b.answer: 1 item is past its date: 1 service visits past their due date.

b.label: FMEAs
b.description: Approved FMEAs are re-read against field failures, nonconformances and process changes. A change means a new revision through review.

b.label: SPC characteristics and control limits
b.description: Whether each characteristic is still measured as planned and its control limits still reflect the process.

b.label: Controlled documents
b.description: Procedures, work instructions and manuals are confirmed current, or revised. Counts from the approval of the current version.

b.label: Policies and handbook
b.description: Each published policy is confirmed current, or revised (a revision can ask everyone to acknowledge it again).

b.label: Expense policy
b.description: Mileage rate, receipt threshold and submission deadline, and the approval rules.

b.label: Training course content
b.description: Course material and quizzes are checked against current procedures. Counts from publication of the current version.

b.label: User access
b.description: Who holds which roles at which sites: leavers removed, roles still needed. Kept for audits (SOX, ISO 27001).

b.label: Approved suppliers
b.description: Re-evaluation of suppliers used in the last two years: performance, certificates, and whether they stay approved (ISO 9001 8.4).

b.label: PM plans
b.description: Tasks, interval and parts still right for the machine, judged against its failures since.

b.label: Critical spares lists
b.description: For each machine with a spares list: critical parts and minimum stock still right.

b.label: Repair templates
b.description: Standard repairs: parts, labor estimate and procedure still match what the job takes.

b.label: Store walk checklists
b.description: Checklist items still match the standards stores are held to.

b.label: Business continuity plans
b.description: Each plan keeps its own review and exercise frequencies; this sets the default for new plans. Reminders come from “Continuity plan reviews and exercises”.

b.label: Sites (properties, stores, plants)
b.description: One row per property, store, plant or warehouse with its address and optional group (portfolio, region, district). Administrators only.

b.label: Departments / cost centers
b.description: Department code and name, optionally the site it belongs to. Approval rules, budgets and expense reports use departments. Heads are chosen in the product after people have signed in.

b.label: Employees / technicians
b.description: Directory records used for technician assignment and labor. Do not import pay rates or other HR-sensitive data here.

b.label: People who sign in, with roles
b.description: Work email, name, the employee number (to link the employee record), a role and the site it applies to. Leave the site blank for all sites. One row per role: repeat the person for a second role. They sign in through the company's identity provider, which finds them by email.

fields.label: Role
fields.description: A role name as shown under Administration, for example Maintenance Manager or Technician

fields.label: Site code
fields.description: Blank = all sites

b.label: Assets / equipment register
b.description: Equipment, components, tools and facility systems. Locations are created from paths like "Bldg 2 > Line 3"; components reference their parent by tag.

fields.label: Location path
fields.description: Hierarchy separated by ">" or "/", e.g. "Building 2 > Line 3". Missing locations are created.

b.label: Parts / spares master
b.description: Maintenance spares and consumables. Load on-hand quantities with the stock_balances target; unmapped columns are kept in custom fields.

fields.label: Purchase unit
fields.description: The unit it is bought in when that is not the stock unit (BOX, CASE, DRUM); with "Stock units per purchase unit"

fields.label: Stock units per purchase unit
fields.description: How many stock units are in one purchase unit (a box of 10: 10)

b.label: Storerooms
b.description: Each place stock is kept: code, name, site. Bins are a column on the stock balances, not locations of their own.

b.label: Stock on hand (opening balances)
b.description: On-hand quantity per part and storeroom, with optional bin and reorder settings. Parts and storerooms must exist first.

fields.label: Lot or serial number
fields.description: Required for lot- or serial-tracked parts; one row per lot

b.label: Equipment parts lists (spares per machine)
b.description: Which spare parts each machine uses, how many are installed, where, and which are critical. Matches parts by part number or manufacturer part number.

b.label: Meter readings
b.description: Readings of hour, cycle or mileage meters per machine: asset tag, meter name, reading, date. Applied oldest first; a reading below an earlier one is refused. The last reading per meter is what meter-based preventive maintenance counts from.

b.label: Preventive maintenance plans
b.description: One row per machine and task: asset tag, task, how often (days, or a word like monthly or "every 6 months"; or a meter and its interval), hours, and when it was last done so the next due date continues the schedule. Machines must be loaded first. A plan that already exists is left as it is.

fields.label: Plan code
fields.description: Optional; made from the asset tag and task when blank

fields.label: How often
fields.description: Days (90), or words: weekly, monthly, quarterly, annual, "every 6 months"

fields.label: Meter
fields.description: For meter-based plans: the meter name, for example hours

b.label: Bills of materials
b.description: Components and quantity per unit for manufactured parts, flat or indented. Lines land on a draft revision for review; parts must exist first.

fields.label: Parent part
fields.description: The part being made. Leave unmapped for indented BOMs that use a level column.

b.label: Work centers
b.description: A machine group, cell or station where operations are done: code, name, site, the machines in it (asset tags separated by semicolons), scheduled hours a week and the number of machines or crews. Machines must be loaded first.

fields.label: Machines (asset tags)
fields.description: Asset tags separated by semicolons or commas

b.label: Routings (operations)
b.description: One row per operation: the part made, operation number, work center, description, setup minutes and run minutes per unit. Parts and work centers must exist first. Operations go on the part's draft revision, alongside its bill of material, for a person to review and release.

b.label: Suppliers / vendors
b.description: Vendor list (code, name, contact, terms). Bank and tax details stay in the accounting system; do not import them.

fields.label: Trades (contractors)
fields.description: Comma or semicolon separated, e.g. "plumbing; hvac"

b.label: Supplier price list
b.description: Price, lead time and supplier part number per supplier and part. Suppliers and parts must exist first. One row per supplier and part.

fields.label: Price unit
fields.description: The unit the price is per, when the supplier sells in boxes, cases or drums; blank means the stock unit

b.label: Open purchase orders
b.description: Orders not yet fully received, one row per line: order number, supplier, part (or description), quantity ordered and already received, price, due date. Suppliers and parts must exist first. Received quantities are history; stock on hand is loaded as a count.

b.label: Supplier delivery history
b.description: Past purchase order lines with due and received dates and rejected quantities, for supplier scorecards. Suppliers must be loaded first.

fields.label: PO and line
fields.description: Unique per supplier, e.g. 4500123-10

b.label: Spend history
b.description: Monthly spend by account from the previous accounting system, for history analysis and budgets. Rows are classified into spend categories through the account mapping or a category column.

fields.label: Site
fields.description: Site code; the import's site when blank

fields.label: Department
fields.description: Department code or name (optional)

fields.label: Spend category
fields.description: Spend category code or name; overrides the account mapping

b.label: Budget lines
b.description: One row per site, department, spend category and month: the budget name and year, then the amount. A sheet with a column per month loads through the "wide to long" option. The budget is created as a draft when it does not exist; approved budgets are not changed.

fields.label: Month
fields.description: January or Jan, or 1 to 12 (calendar month)

b.label: Chart of accounts
b.description: Account number, name and type from the accounting system. Adds to the starter chart; accounts that already have entries keep their type. Set the books up first (Books → Settings).

fields.label: Detail type
fields.description: Optional: bank, accounts receivable, inventory, fixed asset, credit card, accounts payable, cost of goods and so on. Worked out from the name when blank.

b.label: Opening balances (trial balance)
b.description: The previous accounting system's trial balance, as opening balances in the built-in books.

fields.label: Account
fields.description: Account number or name; "1000 · Checking" style labels are matched by either part

fields.label: Account name
fields.description: Used to create an account the chart does not have (with a type)

fields.label: Account type
fields.description: Needed only to create a missing account

fields.label: As of
fields.description: Defaults to the day before the books start

b.label: Bank and card transactions
b.description: Statement lines from your bank or card export, into the books' banking queue to match or categorize.

fields.label: Bank account
fields.description: Account code, name or last four digits; the default bank account when blank

fields.label: Amount (signed)
fields.description: Positive money in, negative money out

b.label: Customers / accounts
b.description: Customer and prospect accounts with an optional primary contact per row. Bank and tax IDs stay in accounting; do not import them.

b.label: Sales items and price list
b.description: Products and services you quote and invoice: code, description, kind, unit, list price, cost, and the part it is made as. A part number links the item to stock and production.

b.label: Sales opportunities
b.description: Your pipeline from the CRM or a spreadsheet: customer, title, stage, amount, expected close and the person who owns it. Customers must exist first. A deal that was lost needs the reason.

b.label: Open customer invoices
b.description: Invoices still unpaid at the cutover date (an aging report): invoice number, customer, dates and the amount still owed. Customers must exist first. Paid history is not needed. With the built-in books, load the trial balance without the receivables line: these invoices provide it.

b.label: Open supplier bills
b.description: Bills still unpaid at the cutover date (a payables aging): supplier, bill number, dates and the amount still owed. Suppliers must exist first. With the built-in books, load the trial balance without the payables line: these bills provide it.

b.label: Customer forecasts
b.description: Quantities per customer, part and month into the customer's draft forecast at the chosen site. Activate the draft after reviewing it.

b.label: Consumables and chemicals usage
b.description: How much of a consumable or chemical a work center uses per machine hour, per part made, or per month. Feeds the material plan and its cost forecast.

fields.label: Work center code
fields.description: Blank for site-wide monthly usage

fields.label: Per (how many hours, parts or months)
fields.description: Default 1

b.label: Rental units (beds, size, market rent)
b.description: Makes existing spaces rentable with their type, bedrooms, bathrooms, size and market rent. Load units as assets (class space) first.

b.label: Leases (rent roll)
b.description: Leases in force or signed for the future, from a rent roll export. Units must be rental units first. Balances owed stay in the old system or accounting; this loads the leases, not the ledger.

b.label: Maintenance history (legacy work orders)
b.description: Closed or open work orders from a previous CMMS, spreadsheet or paper log. Legacy numbers are kept; labor is attached when the technician can be matched.

fields.label: Parts and contractor cost
fields.description: Cost of the job other than in-house labor (parts, outside services); used for repair-or-replace

fields.label: Downtime hours (reference only)
fields.description: Kept as reference on the work order. Import a downtime log to build utilization history.

b.label: Downtime / state log
b.description: Historical machine state intervals (e.g. a downtime spreadsheet) used for availability and utilization history. Overlapping intervals for the same asset are rejected.

b.label: Condition limits (coolers, freezers)
b.description: What is logged on which equipment, with its limits and how often: e.g. walk-in cooler 33–41°F every 12 h. Equipment must exist first.

b.label: Condition readings (temperature logs)
b.description: Readings for condition points already set up on assets (e.g. walk-in cooler 33–41°F). Out-of-limit readings raise requests as they would in the app.

fields.label: Measure
fields.description: Defaults to temperature

b.label: SPC characteristics
b.description: One row per measured characteristic: code, name, unit, nominal and limits, subgroup size, how often, and optionally the part and the gauge. Load these before the measurements.

fields.label: Chart type
fields.description: variables (measurements) or p, np, c, u (counts)

b.label: SPC measurements
b.description: Subgroups of measurements for set-up characteristics (one row per subgroup). Control-chart signals and out-of-tolerance values alert quality as they would when typed in.

fields.label: Values
fields.description: One value, or the subgroup separated by spaces or semicolons

fields.label: Sample size (attribute charts)
fields.description: Parts or units inspected, for p and u charts

b.label: Calibration plans and last calibration
b.description: One row per instrument (already loaded as equipment): how often it is calibrated, the tolerance, and when it was last calibrated, by whom, with the certificate. The next due date continues from the last calibration. Past results are recorded as history: they do not raise nonconformances or take instruments out of service.

fields.label: Calibrate every
fields.description: Days, or words: annual, every 6 months

b.label: Nonconformance history
b.description: Past nonconformance reports (NCR, reject, deviation logs): your number, date, what happened, severity, the part and quantity, the disposition and cost, and when it was closed. Brought in as records for trends and audits; the workflow does not run.

b.label: Safety incident history
b.description: Past incident and near-miss logs: your number, date, what kind, what happened, severity, whether it was recordable, days away or restricted. Brought in as closed records so incident rates and trends cover the earlier years. Personal injury detail is not needed.

b.label: Qualifications (definitions)
b.description: The skills and certificates you track: code, name, how long each stays valid, and whether it is safety critical or needs a practical sign-off. Load these before qualification records.

b.label: Qualification records (legacy training matrix)
b.description: One row per person and qualification, or a wide training matrix (one column per qualification) using the unpivot option. Qualifications must be defined first.

b.label: Earning codes (payroll)
b.description: What hours are called on a timesheet (regular, overtime, holiday, sick) and the code your payroll provider uses for each in its import file.

b.label: Timesheet history
b.description: Past hours: employee number, date, earning code, hours (one row per person, day and code). Brought in as already paid: frozen, never exported to payroll again. Employees and earning codes must exist first.

b.label: Expense categories
b.description: Categories people claim against (meals, lodging, mileage): code, name, per-item and per-day limits, the amount over which a receipt is required.

reminders.when: A corrective, safety, audit, FMEA, continuity, store walk or improvement action is past its due date

reminders.label: Effectiveness checks due
reminders.recipients: Quality staff other than the owner
reminders.when: A corrective action has reached its effectiveness check

reminders.label: Supplier corrective action requests unanswered

reminders.label: Audits coming up or not started
reminders.recipients: The lead auditor and the auditee
reminders.when: An audit is planned within {lead} days, or its date has passed and it has not started

reminders.label: Incidents not yet classified
reminders.when: An incident is still unclassified a day after it was reported

reminders.label: Temporary changes ending
reminders.when: A change record marked temporary (one that has no temporary procedure change of its own, which sends its own alerts at 14, 7, 3, 1 and 0 days) ends within {lead} days, or has passed its end date

reminders.label: Continuity plan reviews and exercises
reminders.when: A plan’s review, or its exercise with none scheduled, is due within {lead} days

reminders.label: Training due
reminders.when: Assigned training is due within {lead} days or overdue

reminders.label: Qualifications expiring
reminders.when: A qualification expires within {lead} days

reminders.label: External certificates expiring
reminders.when: A licence or certificate from an outside body expires within {lead} days

reminders.label: Performance reviews and check-ins due
reminders.recipients: The reviewer (HR when none is assigned)
reminders.when: A review or check-in is due within {lead} days, or overdue, and not yet shared

reminders.label: Performance reviews well overdue
reminders.when: Reviews or check-ins are more than {lead} days overdue (one summary)

reminders.label: Timesheets not submitted
reminders.when: Last week’s timesheet has not been submitted (once per week)

reminders.label: Timesheets waiting for approval
reminders.when: Submitted timesheets are waiting

reminders.label: Late purchase orders
reminders.when: An order is past its expected delivery date

reminders.label: Contractor insurance expiring
reminders.when: A contractor’s certificate of insurance expires within {lead} days (work cannot be sent to them after it lapses)

reminders.label: Supplier invoices waiting for approval
reminders.when: Captured supplier invoices are waiting for a second person

reminders.label: Overdue customer invoices
reminders.when: Customer invoices are past their due date

reminders.label: Accounting sync problems
reminders.when: Items sent to the accounting system failed and are parked

reminders.label: Next year’s budget not started
reminders.when: The next fiscal year starts within {lead} days and has no budget yet

reminders.label: Follow-up tasks due
reminders.when: A sales or collections follow-up is due today or overdue

reminders.label: Quotes about to expire
reminders.when: A sent quote with no decision is {lead} days from expiring, 2 days from expiring, or lapsed yesterday (one notice each; the same series the daily job has always sent)

reminders.label: Lots expiring
reminders.when: Usable stock in a lot expires within {lead} days

reminders.label: Store walks not done
reminders.recipients: People who conduct walks at the site
reminders.when: A site that has store walks has had none completed in {lead} days

reminders.label: Leases ending and unit turns late
reminders.when: Leases end within {lead} days without renewal, or unit turns are past their target

b.label: FMEAs
b.description: Approved FMEAs are re-read against field failures, nonconformances and process changes. A change means a new revision through review.

b.label: SPC characteristics and control limits
b.description: Whether each characteristic is still measured as planned and its control limits still reflect the process.

b.label: Controlled documents
b.description: Procedures, work instructions and manuals are confirmed current, or revised. Counts from the approval of the current version.

b.label: Policies and handbook
b.description: Each published policy is confirmed current, or revised (a revision can ask everyone to acknowledge it again).

b.label: Expense policy
b.description: Mileage rate, receipt threshold and submission deadline, and the approval rules.

b.label: Training course content
b.description: Course material and quizzes are checked against current procedures. Counts from publication of the current version.

b.label: User access
b.description: Who holds which roles at which sites: leavers removed, roles still needed. Kept for audits (SOX, ISO 27001).

b.label: Approved suppliers
b.description: Re-evaluation of suppliers used in the last two years: performance, certificates, and whether they stay approved (ISO 9001 8.4).

b.label: PM plans
b.description: Tasks, interval and parts still right for the machine, judged against its failures since.

b.label: Critical spares lists
b.description: For each machine with a spares list: critical parts and minimum stock still right.

b.label: Repair templates
b.description: Standard repairs: parts, labor estimate and procedure still match what the job takes.

b.label: Store walk checklists
b.description: Checklist items still match the standards stores are held to.

b.label: Business continuity plans
b.description: Each plan keeps its own review and exercise frequencies; this sets the default for new plans. Reminders come from “Continuity plan reviews and exercises”.

categories.label: Rows of finished imports
categories.description: The staged rows of an import, holding the values from the uploaded file. The import summary (file name, mapping, counts) stays. Imports never committed are cancelled after the same period.

categories.label: Read notifications
categories.description: Notifications a person has read, counted from when they read them.

categories.label: Unread notifications
categories.description: Notifications nobody opened. The records they point to are not affected.

categories.label: Sent emails
categories.description: Copies of digests and reminders that were sent or failed. Emails still waiting to be sent are never removed.

categories.label: Unsaved form entries
categories.description: What people typed into a form and never saved or discarded (D-164), counted from the last change. Saved records are not affected.

categories.label: Expired sign-in tokens
categories.description: Sign-in tokens past their expiry or revoked. Unfinished single sign-on attempts are removed after a day.

fixed.label: Saved replies for retried requests
fixed.description: Lets a phone that lost its connection resend a change without doing it twice.

kept: The audit log (tamper-evident, never changed or removed)

b.label: Sites (properties, stores, plants)
b.description: One row per property, store, plant or warehouse with its address and optional group (portfolio, region, district). Administrators only.

b.label: Departments / cost centers
b.description: Department code and name, optionally the site it belongs to. Approval rules, budgets and expense reports use departments. Heads are chosen in the product after people have signed in.

b.label: Employees / technicians
b.description: Directory records used for technician assignment and labor. Do not import pay rates or other HR-sensitive data here.

b.label: People who sign in, with roles
b.description: Work email, name, the employee number (to link the employee record), a role and the site it applies to. Leave the site blank for all sites. One row per role: repeat the person for a second role. They sign in through the company's identity provider, which finds them by email.

fields.label: Role
fields.description: A role name as shown under Administration, for example Maintenance Manager or Technician

fields.label: Site code
fields.description: Blank = all sites

b.label: Assets / equipment register
b.description: Equipment, components, tools and facility systems. Locations are created from paths like "Bldg 2 > Line 3"; components reference their parent by tag.

fields.label: Location path
fields.description: Hierarchy separated by ">" or "/", e.g. "Building 2 > Line 3". Missing locations are created.

b.label: Parts / spares master
b.description: Maintenance spares and consumables. Load on-hand quantities with the stock_balances target; unmapped columns are kept in custom fields.

fields.label: Purchase unit
fields.description: The unit it is bought in when that is not the stock unit (BOX, CASE, DRUM); with "Stock units per purchase unit"

fields.label: Stock units per purchase unit
fields.description: How many stock units are in one purchase unit (a box of 10: 10)

b.label: Storerooms
b.description: Each place stock is kept: code, name, site. Bins are a column on the stock balances, not locations of their own.

b.label: Stock on hand (opening balances)
b.description: On-hand quantity per part and storeroom, with optional bin and reorder settings. Parts and storerooms must exist first.

fields.label: Lot or serial number
fields.description: Required for lot- or serial-tracked parts; one row per lot

b.label: Equipment parts lists (spares per machine)
b.description: Which spare parts each machine uses, how many are installed, where, and which are critical. Matches parts by part number or manufacturer part number.

b.label: Meter readings
b.description: Readings of hour, cycle or mileage meters per machine: asset tag, meter name, reading, date. Applied oldest first; a reading below an earlier one is refused. The last reading per meter is what meter-based preventive maintenance counts from.

b.label: Preventive maintenance plans
b.description: One row per machine and task: asset tag, task, how often (days, or a word like monthly or "every 6 months"; or a meter and its interval), hours, and when it was last done so the next due date continues the schedule. Machines must be loaded first. A plan that already exists is left as it is.

fields.label: Plan code
fields.description: Optional; made from the asset tag and task when blank

fields.label: How often
fields.description: Days (90), or words: weekly, monthly, quarterly, annual, "every 6 months"

fields.label: Meter
fields.description: For meter-based plans: the meter name, for example hours

b.label: Bills of materials
b.description: Components and quantity per unit for manufactured parts, flat or indented. Lines land on a draft revision for review; parts must exist first.

fields.label: Parent part
fields.description: The part being made. Leave unmapped for indented BOMs that use a level column.

b.label: Work centers
b.description: A machine group, cell or station where operations are done: code, name, site, the machines in it (asset tags separated by semicolons), scheduled hours a week and the number of machines or crews. Machines must be loaded first.

fields.label: Machines (asset tags)
fields.description: Asset tags separated by semicolons or commas

b.label: Routings (operations)
b.description: One row per operation: the part made, operation number, work center, description, setup minutes and run minutes per unit. Parts and work centers must exist first. Operations go on the part's draft revision, alongside its bill of material, for a person to review and release.

b.label: Suppliers / vendors
b.description: Vendor list (code, name, contact, terms). Bank and tax details stay in the accounting system; do not import them.

fields.label: Trades (contractors)
fields.description: Comma or semicolon separated, e.g. "plumbing; hvac"

b.label: Supplier price list
b.description: Price, lead time and supplier part number per supplier and part. Suppliers and parts must exist first. One row per supplier and part.

fields.label: Price unit
fields.description: The unit the price is per, when the supplier sells in boxes, cases or drums; blank means the stock unit

b.label: Open purchase orders
b.description: Orders not yet fully received, one row per line: order number, supplier, part (or description), quantity ordered and already received, price, due date. Suppliers and parts must exist first. Received quantities are history; stock on hand is loaded as a count.

b.label: Supplier delivery history
b.description: Past purchase order lines with due and received dates and rejected quantities, for supplier scorecards. Suppliers must be loaded first.

fields.label: PO and line
fields.description: Unique per supplier, e.g. 4500123-10

b.label: Spend history
b.description: Monthly spend by account from the previous accounting system, for history analysis and budgets. Rows are classified into spend categories through the account mapping or a category column.

fields.label: Site
fields.description: Site code; the import's site when blank

fields.label: Department
fields.description: Department code or name (optional)

fields.label: Spend category
fields.description: Spend category code or name; overrides the account mapping

b.label: Budget lines
b.description: One row per site, department, spend category and month: the budget name and year, then the amount. A sheet with a column per month loads through the "wide to long" option. The budget is created as a draft when it does not exist; approved budgets are not changed.

fields.label: Month
fields.description: January or Jan, or 1 to 12 (calendar month)

b.label: Chart of accounts
b.description: Account number, name and type from the accounting system. Adds to the starter chart; accounts that already have entries keep their type. Set the books up first (Books → Settings).

fields.label: Detail type
fields.description: Optional: bank, accounts receivable, inventory, fixed asset, credit card, accounts payable, cost of goods and so on. Worked out from the name when blank.

b.label: Opening balances (trial balance)
b.description: The previous accounting system's trial balance, as opening balances in the built-in books.

fields.label: Account
fields.description: Account number or name; "1000 · Checking" style labels are matched by either part

fields.label: Account name
fields.description: Used to create an account the chart does not have (with a type)

fields.label: Account type
fields.description: Needed only to create a missing account

fields.label: As of
fields.description: Defaults to the day before the books start

b.label: Bank and card transactions
b.description: Statement lines from your bank or card export, into the books' banking queue to match or categorize.

fields.label: Bank account
fields.description: Account code, name or last four digits; the default bank account when blank

fields.label: Amount (signed)
fields.description: Positive money in, negative money out

b.label: Customers / accounts
b.description: Customer and prospect accounts with an optional primary contact per row. Bank and tax IDs stay in accounting; do not import them.

b.label: Sales items and price list
b.description: Products and services you quote and invoice: code, description, kind, unit, list price, cost, and the part it is made as. A part number links the item to stock and production.

b.label: Sales opportunities
b.description: Your pipeline from the CRM or a spreadsheet: customer, title, stage, amount, expected close and the person who owns it. Customers must exist first. A deal that was lost needs the reason.

b.label: Open customer invoices
b.description: Invoices still unpaid at the cutover date (an aging report): invoice number, customer, dates and the amount still owed. Customers must exist first. Paid history is not needed. With the built-in books, load the trial balance without the receivables line: these invoices provide it.

b.label: Open supplier bills
b.description: Bills still unpaid at the cutover date (a payables aging): supplier, bill number, dates and the amount still owed. Suppliers must exist first. With the built-in books, load the trial balance without the payables line: these bills provide it.

b.label: Customer forecasts
b.description: Quantities per customer, part and month into the customer's draft forecast at the chosen site. Activate the draft after reviewing it.

b.label: Consumables and chemicals usage
b.description: How much of a consumable or chemical a work center uses per machine hour, per part made, or per month. Feeds the material plan and its cost forecast.

fields.label: Work center code
fields.description: Blank for site-wide monthly usage

fields.label: Per (how many hours, parts or months)
fields.description: Default 1

b.label: Rental units (beds, size, market rent)
b.description: Makes existing spaces rentable with their type, bedrooms, bathrooms, size and market rent. Load units as assets (class space) first.

b.label: Leases (rent roll)
b.description: Leases in force or signed for the future, from a rent roll export. Units must be rental units first. Balances owed stay in the old system or accounting; this loads the leases, not the ledger.

b.label: Maintenance history (legacy work orders)
b.description: Closed or open work orders from a previous CMMS, spreadsheet or paper log. Legacy numbers are kept; labor is attached when the technician can be matched.

fields.label: Parts and contractor cost
fields.description: Cost of the job other than in-house labor (parts, outside services); used for repair-or-replace

fields.label: Downtime hours (reference only)
fields.description: Kept as reference on the work order. Import a downtime log to build utilization history.

b.label: Downtime / state log
b.description: Historical machine state intervals (e.g. a downtime spreadsheet) used for availability and utilization history. Overlapping intervals for the same asset are rejected.

b.label: Condition limits (coolers, freezers)
b.description: What is logged on which equipment, with its limits and how often: e.g. walk-in cooler 33–41°F every 12 h. Equipment must exist first.

b.label: Condition readings (temperature logs)
b.description: Readings for condition points already set up on assets (e.g. walk-in cooler 33–41°F). Out-of-limit readings raise requests as they would in the app.

fields.label: Measure
fields.description: Defaults to temperature

b.label: SPC characteristics
b.description: One row per measured characteristic: code, name, unit, nominal and limits, subgroup size, how often, and optionally the part and the gauge. Load these before the measurements.

fields.label: Chart type
fields.description: variables (measurements) or p, np, c, u (counts)

b.label: SPC measurements
b.description: Subgroups of measurements for set-up characteristics (one row per subgroup). Control-chart signals and out-of-tolerance values alert quality as they would when typed in.

fields.label: Values
fields.description: One value, or the subgroup separated by spaces or semicolons

fields.label: Sample size (attribute charts)
fields.description: Parts or units inspected, for p and u charts

b.label: Calibration plans and last calibration
b.description: One row per instrument (already loaded as equipment): how often it is calibrated, the tolerance, and when it was last calibrated, by whom, with the certificate. The next due date continues from the last calibration. Past results are recorded as history: they do not raise nonconformances or take instruments out of service.

fields.label: Calibrate every
fields.description: Days, or words: annual, every 6 months

b.label: Nonconformance history
b.description: Past nonconformance reports (NCR, reject, deviation logs): your number, date, what happened, severity, the part and quantity, the disposition and cost, and when it was closed. Brought in as records for trends and audits; the workflow does not run.

b.label: Safety incident history
b.description: Past incident and near-miss logs: your number, date, what kind, what happened, severity, whether it was recordable, days away or restricted. Brought in as closed records so incident rates and trends cover the earlier years. Personal injury detail is not needed.

b.label: Qualifications (definitions)
b.description: The skills and certificates you track: code, name, how long each stays valid, and whether it is safety critical or needs a practical sign-off. Load these before qualification records.

b.label: Qualification records (legacy training matrix)
b.description: One row per person and qualification, or a wide training matrix (one column per qualification) using the unpivot option. Qualifications must be defined first.

b.label: Earning codes (payroll)
b.description: What hours are called on a timesheet (regular, overtime, holiday, sick) and the code your payroll provider uses for each in its import file.

b.label: Timesheet history
b.description: Past hours: employee number, date, earning code, hours (one row per person, day and code). Brought in as already paid: frozen, never exported to payroll again. Employees and earning codes must exist first.

b.label: Expense categories
b.description: Categories people claim against (meals, lodging, mileage): code, name, per-item and per-day limits, the amount over which a receipt is required.
